spots.name: Ball's Pyramid
spots.reason: 29 km from the island's centre, outside its 15 km span (about 11 km radius); the span would have to balloon to hold it. It has no landing and is reached only by boat or dive trip from Lord Howe, so it is standalone whether or not the island destination is accepted; the island's bio/tips should mention the boat trips.
spots.bio: The world's tallest sea stack, 23 km offshore, seen on boat tours from the island and reached by dive trips.

photo.file: Balls Pyramid, Lord Howe Marine Park 1008.jpg
photo.skeptic_note: Colour 2014 sea-level view of the stack with surf, subject centred, strong; p40 0.40 mean 0.52. Licence not read (API errored): Lens to confirm.

spots.coordinates_note: Wikipedia sea-stack point, correct for an offshore feature.
spots.ticketUrl_note: Sold by many operators (boat tour, dive trip): likely no single ticketUrl.

new_destinations.name: Lord Howe Island
new_destinations.coordinates_source: approximate township centre between the museum (OSM -31.52791,159.06655) and Lagoon Beach; to be confirmed in Pipeline C
new_destinations.access: By plane (Sydney, Brisbane, Port Macquarie); no other access
new_destinations.note: Proposal only, listed for the owner, not added. It needs description, three reasons with photos, tips, best months and a header (WRITING.md). IANA zone Australia/Lord_Howe confirmed (UTC+10:30, DST +11). Fifteen kept places is enough to fill a visit; the island is a UNESCO World Heritage Area with its own accommodation and tourism infrastructure.

if_destination_declined: Every entry has standalone_fallback (id, country Australia, AU, Oceania, Australia/Lord_Howe); Ball's Pyramid is standalone either way. Without the destination the map would show 13 standalone pins on an 11 km island, and the country sheet still needs another AU destination (Sydney exists).
